Subject: PO vs Card — follow-up / next steps

Hi Samantha / Tom —

Great to meet earlier — thanks for the time. Quick recap and next steps so we stay aligned on procurement and billing options for the PoC:

- Procurement constraints: you mentioned FinOpsCo prefers POs and net-30/60 terms for vendors, but the revenue team is OK with a temporary card payment for trials under certain thresholds.
- Marketplace path: Tom asked about AWS Marketplace availability as an alternative procurement route that can speed onboarding and simplify billing.
- Vendor onboarding: Procurement will need our vendor questionnaire, W-9, and standard SLA attachments.

Proposed next steps:
1) I will send a short action plan with the items Procurement needs from Redwood (vendor docs + estimated PoC billing).
2) If Procurement needs a PO, Marissa can coordinate contract routing and billing terms.
3) If you want to go fast we can accept card for the initial trial (we can invoice Procurement later when PO is issued).

Please confirm which path you prefer (PO-first vs card-to-start) and any internal thresholds we should know about (e.g., approvals for vendors under $5k/yr).

Attachments referenced: vendor questionnaire / standard docs (I can attach these in a follow-up).

Thanks —

Subject: Re: PO vs Card — follow-up / next steps

Thanks Lauren — helpful summary. A few clarifications from procurement's side:

- Our standard policy is to put vendors on PO with net-30 or net-60 depending on the vendor size and category.
- We can make exceptions for card payments to expedite trials, but that typically requires approval from our AP manager if expected spend > $2k/month or > $5k/year.
- For marketplace: if Redwood is available on AWS Marketplace (or GCP/Azure equivalent), Procurement prefers that route because it simplifies chargebacks and is pre-approved in our vendor catalog.

Two asks before we move forward:
1) Can you send your vendor onboarding packet (W-9, vendor questionnaire, and SOC2 cert info if available)?
2) What is the expected PoC spend (estimate of total card charge if we decide to run on card)?

If you can get those over today we can try to fast-track the PO, otherwise we'll route the card approval.

Thanks,
Samantha Lee
Director, Procurement | FinOpsCo
samantha.lee@finopsco.com

Hi Samantha — looping in a couple notes from sales ops and procurement intake that should help:

- Vendor packet: see attached "Redwood_Marketplace_Procurement_Guide.pdf" — includes W-9, our standard vendor questionnaire, SOC2 summary, and contact for security evidence. If Procurement needs full SOC2 artifact we'll coordinate an NDA + secure transfer.
- Marketplace: we are listed in AWS Marketplace for our hosted API (metered billing), which often clears procurement faster. If your team wants to use Marketplace we can provide the SKU and the marketplace purchase order flow.
- PO vs Card practicalities: for PoCs under $5k total, card is the fastest option (no PO required). For enterprise PoCs >$5k or multi-region dedicated capacity, Procurement often prefers PO so they can set up terms and vendor codes.
